title: fix(metadata-protocol,runtime): a seed row a person deleted is no longer inserted again by the next seed replay (per-organization record of landed seed keys)
body:
Fixes #31021

Clause-②: yes (widening)
Metadata-protocol: semantic
Skills-docs: follow-up #31090

Claim: 6701308503 (File surface amended in review of this PR) · Branch: `claude/issue-31021-seed-landed-keys` · File surface: the seed loader and its tests, AppPlugin's seed loads, the new platform object `sys_seed_landed_key` with its registration and the regenerated `scripts/platform-object-tenancy-census.json`, one changeset, and the three lines the object forces outside the server package trees: the roster line `'sys_seed_landed_key'` in `PLATFORM_OBJECTS_BY_PACKAGE['platform-objects']` (`packages/spec`), its `ORGANIZATION_OWNERSHIP_INVENTORY` row (`packages/cli`), and its entry in plugin-audit's `SKIP_OBJECTS` · Spec review: the roster line owes a `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` review, requested from `domain:spec#1`

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：平台为每个组织记下哪些种子行已经落过地，记录存在新的系统对象 `sys_seed_landed_key` 里。之后启动或升级重放种子时，被人删掉的种子行不再按新 id 插回来，升级新加的种子行照常插入。
- 为什么改：cloud 实测，用户删掉的示例数据在下次装包或升级时会回来（cloud#3657）。自托管的 `objectstack serve` 每次启动重放种子，问题一样。平台的问题在平台处理。
- 风险与回滚：只有 AppPlugin 的三条种子加载会读写这份记录（启动种子、按组织重放、dev 热加载），包发布、市场安装、重新灌样例数据等其他入口不变。记录写失败只报一次 error，不影响种子行本身。新对象带来的三行也在本 PR：spec 平台对象名册加一行、CLI 组织归属清单加一行、审计跳过表加一行（记录行不进审计日志）。回滚就是 revert 本 PR，多出的表无害。
- 先看：`packages/metadata-protocol/src/seed-loader.ts` 的 `isWithdrawnRow`（不再插回被删的行）、`resolveReferenceItem` 的 `withdrawn` 分支（指向被删行的引用不报错）、`recordLandedKeys`（同一轮写记录）；`packages/runtime/src/app-plugin.ts` 的 `seedLoaderOptionsFor` 和 replayer 的 `reseed` 选项；`packages/spec/src/system/constants/platform-object-names.ts` 名册那一行。
- 两分钟验证：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/metadata-protocol exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/seed-loader-landed-ids.test.ts -t "31021"`，预期 13 条全绿：删掉的行不回来、改过的行不动、升级新行照插、reseed 能恢复、记录按组织分开。
- 需要你做的：无，席位落地（spec 名册那一行由 `domain:spec#1` 做契约复审）。

## What changes

**`@objectstack/metadata-protocol` — `SeedLoaderService`** (`src/seed-loader.ts`)

- New constructor option `landedKeys: 'honour' | 'reseed'` on `SeedLoaderServiceOptions`. A loader built without it reads and writes nothing new, so every other caller behaves as before.
- When it is set, the loader opens a per-load record for the organization the load seeds. That organization is `config.organizationId`, or the install's sole organization (`fallbackOrgId`, the `single` posture's Default Organization on a `serve` boot). If the load seeds no organization, it keeps no record and says so once at `info`. If `sys_seed_landed_key` is not registered, it keeps no record and says so once at `warn`.
- For an `upsert` or `ignore` dataset, the loader records the key of every row the dataset lands, in the same pass that writes it. A landed row is one that was inserted, updated, or matched and left alone. The key is the dataset's `externalId` field names with the values the row was matched by, JSON-encoded, for example `[["name","Acme"]]`. JSON keeps the stored key free of the in-memory NUL joiner. An `id` key is recorded under the AUTHORED id, not the per-organization id a replay may assign (#21665).
- **The rule:** a keyed row the load cannot find is inserted only when its key never landed in that organization. A recorded key whose row is gone is not inserted again. Such a row is counted as `skipped`, and one `info` line per load names how many and on which objects.
- **References to a removed row:** after every database probe misses, `resolveReferenceItem` answers `withdrawn` when the record names the target key as landed. A single link is left unwritten: a matched row keeps what it holds, and a created row lands without the link. A multi-value link keeps the elements that still resolve. A row whose own `externalId` holds such a reference is withdrawn with it. Nothing is deferred and nothing is reported unresolved, so a replay after a person's delete still reads `success: true`. Pass 2 settles a deferred element the same way. When the record is in use, the key's own references now resolve before any other reference, so a withdrawn row resolves and defers nothing.
- A record read that fails for any reason other than a missing table propagates, the same as `loadExistingRecords`. A record write that fails is reported once at `error` and fails neither the rows nor the load. The next load records every row that is still present.

**`@objectstack/runtime` — `AppPlugin`** (`src/app-plugin.ts`)

- All three seed loads AppPlugin runs honour the record: the boot (inline) seed that `objectstack serve` and `os start` run, the per-organization `seed-replayer` that hosts and `sys_organization` insert call, and the dev hot-reload seeder.
- **The door for a deliberate re-seed:** `seed-replayer(organizationId, { reseed: true })`. It inserts every missing row, including the ones a person removed, and records them again. A new database starts with an empty record, and deleting an organization cascades its record.

**`@objectstack/platform-objects` — `sys_seed_landed_key`** (`src/system/sys-seed-landed-key.object.ts`)

- `SysSeedLandedKey` is organization-owned. Its organization column cascades. It is engine-owned, gated by `manage_platform_settings`, and has no data API and no lifecycle block, so it is durable. It has one non-unique index on `(organization_id, object_name)`. `PlatformObjectsPlugin` registers it and the package exports it. `scripts/platform-object-tenancy-census.json` is regenerated: 97 registered, 50 in reach.

**The three lines the object forces**

- `@objectstack/spec`: `PLATFORM_OBJECTS_BY_PACKAGE['platform-objects']` lists `'sys_seed_landed_key'` in sorted position. `PLATFORM_PROVIDED_OBJECT_NAMES` and `isPlatformProvidedObjectName` follow, so a stack that references the object now resolves it instead of drawing the unknown-platform-name advisory. Nothing that was accepted is refused. This follows the `sys_lifecycle_state` precedent (#30751).
- `@objectstack/cli`: `ORGANIZATION_OWNERSHIP_INVENTORY` has a row for the object: `census: platform-census-main`, fate 3 `attribution`, `anchors: []`, cited `(in reach, added since the first census)` with `D10_SINGLE`. This is the inventory's disposition for an organization-owned, engine-written table, the same as `sys_recycle_bin` and `sys_connector_connection`. The loader writes every row with the organization its load seeds and writes none without one, so a NULL row has no producer, and a key names its seed row by natural key, so no parent row anchors it. The `column-drop` fate of `sys_lifecycle_state` applies only to tenant-less tables, and this one is not tenant-less.
- `@objectstack/plugin-audit`: `SKIP_OBJECTS` lists `'sys_seed_landed_key'` beside `sys_lifecycle_state`. Recording which seed rows landed writes no `sys_audit_log` or `sys_activity` row of its own; the seeded rows themselves stay audited.

Why a new object rather than existing state: no existing platform object fits. `sys_setting` is the settings K/V store, and its own header refuses internal state. `sys_migration` and `sys_lifecycle_state` are deployment-level and tenant-less. `sys_metadata_activation` is an activation boolean per artifact. `sys_recycle_bin` is reaped after its retention window, so a removed row would come back after it. The record has to sit in the same database as the rows it describes, scoped by organization. That is why it is not a host seam like the package-state store (#31008).

## Tests

<details><summary>New pins and their runs (loader, AppPlugin and object at d1abef04; the three forced lines at 6a1892ec)</summary>

- `packages/metadata-protocol/src/seed-loader-landed-ids.test.ts` — a new top-level describe with 13 cases in the existing landed-ids harness. They cover: the key recorded per organization and recorded once; a deleted row not re-inserted by a reboot or by a seed-union change, while the upgrade's new row lands; the same under `upsert`; an edited row and a renamed key untouched; a reference to a removed row left as it is (single and multi-value, no error, no deferral); a row keyed on a removed row withdrawn with it; the `reseed` door; isolation between organizations, with a new organization getting the whole seed; an `id`-keyed row recorded under its authored id; no organization or no registered object keeping no record, saying so once; a loader not asked neither reading nor writing; a failed record write reported once at `error` with the load succeeding; a failed record read stopping the load.
- `packages/runtime/src/app-plugin.seed-landed.test.ts` — a new top-level describe with 2 cases. In the first, `serve`'s inline seed with the sole Default Organization keeps a deleted row deleted across a reboot and an upgrade, and the upgrade's new row lands. In the second, the per-organization replayer keeps the record per organization, and `{ reseed: true }` brings the row back.
- `packages/platform-objects/src/plugin.test.ts` — the registered list now includes the object, and its shape is pinned.
- The roster line is pinned both ways by the existing `packages/spec/src/system/constants/platform-object-names.test.ts`, and the inventory row by the existing `packages/cli/src/utils/organization-ownership-inventory.test.ts`, which enumerates that roster.

## Acceptance notes

**The `SKIP_OBJECTS` entry has no case of its own.** The amended File surface names the line, not `audit-writers.test.ts`, so no `sys_seed_landed_key` case was added beside the `sys_lifecycle_state` one. `audit-writers.test.ts` and the two read-visibility suites stay green with the entry.

**Boundaries, by design:**

- Only AppPlugin's loads ask for the record. These doors keep today's behaviour: the package-publish apply (`protocol-publish-batch.ts`), runtime `domains/packages.ts`, and cloud-connection install-local's install, heal, reseed and purge. The install-local reseed is the existing "restore sample data" door, and it never reads the record, so it still restores. A row it restores is present, so later replays leave it alone.
- A row deleted BEFORE this lands has no record. The first replay after the upgrade inserts it once more and records it, the same as today. From then on, a delete is remembered.
- A composition with no organization object keeps no record and says so at `info`.
- A seeded object with tenancy disabled is recorded under the load's organization. An organization that never landed the global row, such as a new organization's first replay, inserts it again.
- `Metadata-protocol: semantic`: the meaning of an authored `mode: 'ignore'` or `mode: 'upsert'` on replay changes. A removed row whose key landed is no longer "a row the dataset is missing". No key is added. The roster line would make the kind `added` as well, and `semantic` outranks `added`. `Clause-②: yes (widening)`: `SysSeedLandedKey` is a new export of `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `SeedLoaderServiceOptions` gains `landedKeys`, and the platform object roster lists one more real object. There is no new schema option and no new error code. The changeset is `minor` for every package this diff moves (metadata-protocol, runtime, platform-objects, spec, cli, plugin-audit), because a kind other than `none` takes `minor` (AGENTS.md, Post-Task Checklist step 3; #30751's changeset did the same).
- The docs owe a follow-up. `content/docs/data-modeling/seed-data.mdx` (Import Modes) still says `ignore` inserts "a record whose row is missing". It should say that a removed seed row is not inserted again, and name the reseed door.
- Hosted: the card's cloud rig reaches the loader through AppPlugin's `seed-replayer`. This session has no read access to objectstack-ai/cloud, so the `ArtifactKernelFactory` call site is NOT MEASURED here. `packages/cli` has no seed call site of its own: `serve` seeds through AppPlugin, and `serve.ts` only reads the settlement.
